item.mechanism: Increased lattice disorder at high temperatures leads to higher tangential forces and friction coefficients due to the material's inability to maintain ordered slip planes.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Friction simulation at 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K; indenter speed 10 m/s; depth 10 Å
item.supporting_observation: Tangential force shows a slow increasing trend with temperature; friction coefficients gradually increase, especially from 900 K to 1200 K.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is specific to the FeNiCrCoCu composition; the authors note they did not analyze the effect of changing element proportions.
quotes: With the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process.
With the increase of temperature, the friction coefficients gradually increased, and the fluctuation range also continued to increase.
This is because the high temperature leads to the increase in the proportion of disordered atoms in the material.

item.mechanism: A reduction in dislocation density between 300 K and 600 K results in an increase in elastic modulus, despite similar hardness levels.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Nanoindentation and friction simulation at 300 K and 600 K; loading speed 10 m/s
item.supporting_observation: Elastic modulus increased from 173 GPa to 219 GPa; dislocation density at 600 K is significantly reduced compared to 300 K.
item.scope_limits: This trend reverses at 900 K and 1200 K where dislocation density increases rapidly, causing modulus to drop.
quotes: However, the dislocation density at 600 K is significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K, resulting in an increase of the elastic modulus of the material from 173 GPa to 219 GPa.
The density of dislocations at 600 K was significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K, resulting in the increase of the elastic modulus of the material from 173 GPa to 219 GPa.
At temperatures of 900 K and 1200 K, the densities of dislocations increased rapidly, resulting in a significant decrease in the elastic modulus of the material.

item.mechanism: Thermal softening at high temperatures causes a significant decrease in normal force and hardness, leading to a sharp decline in wear resistance.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Friction simulation at temperatures reaching 900 K and 1200 K
item.supporting_observation: Normal force decreases significantly; hardness drops from 17.4 GPa at 900 K to 8.6 GPa at 1200 K; wear resistance decreases sharply at 900 K.
item.scope_limits: The sharp decrease in wear resistance is specifically noted at 900 K and above; the alloy remains relatively stable up to 900 K.
quotes: When the temperature reaches 900 K, the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating decreases sharply.
When the temperature was raised to 900 K, there was a large decrease from 17.4 GPa to 10.2 GPa.
The value of the normal force decreases greatly due to thermal softening with the increase of temperature.

item.mechanism: Deformation mechanism shifts from stacking fault formation to lattice disorder and melting as temperature approaches the matrix melting point.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.supporting_observation: At 1200 K, a large number of disordered structures appeared and began to melt in the Cu matrix; stacking faults began to decrease.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism is dominant at 1200 K; at lower temperatures (300-900 K), the structure remains largely FCC with stacking faults.
quotes: Due to the softening of the lattice with increasing temperature, the deformation mechanism transformed from stacking faults to lattice disorder.
During the friction process, a large number of disordered structures appeared and began to melt, and the stacking faults also began to decrease at 1200 K.
At a temperature of 1200 K, the proportion of disordered lattice structures increases rapidly, resulting in a significant decrease in the normal force.

item.mechanism: Disordered structures and melting in the Cu matrix at high temperatures hinder the generation of long dislocation lines, leading to short, uniformly distributed dislocations.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.supporting_observation: In the Cu matrix at 1200 K, there were uniformly distributed short dislocations, and no longer a long dislocation line.
item.scope_limits: This phenomenon is specific to the Cu matrix under high temperature; the coating itself showed continuous line defects.
quotes: However, there was a uniform dense distribution of short dislocations, and no longer a long dislocation line in the Cu matrix.
This might be due to a large number of surface defects in the Cu matrix under the high temperature environment, which hindered the generation of line defect dislocation.
This might be due to the damage of the contact surface caused by the penetration of the coating into the matrix under the pressure of the indenter at high temperature.

item.mechanism: At 300 K and 600 K, the ordered lattice structure remains stable, resulting in similar hardness values despite changes in dislocation density.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Friction and nanoindentation at 300 K and 600 K
item.supporting_observation: Hardness is basically the same at 300 K and 600 K; the ordered lattice structure is basically the same at these temperatures.
item.scope_limits: This stability does not extend to 900 K and 1200 K where hardness decreases significantly.
quotes: At 300 K and 600 K, the ordered lattice structure of the high entropy alloy coating material is basically the same, and thus its hardness is basically the same.
The hardnesses of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating are basically the same at 300 K and 600 K.
At 300 K, 600 K, and 900 K, the ordered lattice structures of the high entropy alloy coating material are basically the same.

item.mechanism: The friction coefficient increases with temperature because the tangential force remains stable while the normal force decreases significantly due to thermal softening.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Friction simulation at 900 K to 1200 K
item.supporting_observation: Tangential force in the friction process was basically stable, resulting in a significant increase in the friction coefficient of the material.
item.scope_limits: This specific mechanism of stable tangential force vs. decreasing normal force is highlighted for the 900-1200 K range.
quotes: The friction depth of the indenter was less than the thickness of the high entropy alloy coating, and the value of the tangential force in the friction process was basically stable, resulting in a significant increase in the friction coefficient of the material.
When the temperature reaches 1200 K, the change of the normal force amplitude increases, and the value of the positive force decreases by about 40 nN from that found below 900 K.
The friction coefficients increased with the temperature, especially when the temperature reached 1200 K.

item.mechanism: Atomic disorder increases with temperature starting at 600 K, which leads to decreasing hardness.
item.system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a Cu matrix
item.operating_conditions: Nanoindentation and friction simulation from 300 K to 1200 K
item.supporting_observation: Hardness decreased from 17.4 GPa at 900 K to 8.6 GPa at 1200 K; degree of atomic disorder increases with temperature when reaching 600 K.
item.scope_limits: The authors note that hardness was basically the same at 300 K and 600 K, suggesting the disorder effect on hardness becomes dominant later.
quotes: When the temperature was raised from 900 K to 1200 K, the hardness decreased slightly, from 10.2 GPa to 8.6 GPa.
